question.text: What is 'Delta' and how does it differ for call and put options?

answer.text: Delta measures the change in option premium per unit change in underlying price — call delta is positive (0 to +1), put delta is negative (-1 to 0)
Delta measures the time decay of an option premium
Delta is always +1 for calls and -1 for puts regardless of moneyness
Delta measures the sensitivity of option premium to volatility changes

explanation.text: The Logic: Delta is the change in option premium per unit change in the underlying. A long call's delta ranges from 0 to +1; a long put's delta ranges from -1 to 0. Delta is also used as the hedge ratio for delta-neutral portfolios. The Trap: Time decay is theta, not delta. Volatility sensitivity is vega. Delta values of +1 or -1 occur only for deep ITM options. Note: Delta is distinct from theta (time decay) and vega (volatility sensitivity).
